artifacts.summary: Confirms the flake's root cause (redundant wall-clock assertion with ~0.4s headroom inside a subprocess-injected source string) and the scanner's exact blind spot (clock-read/bound-assert pair lives inside a same-function string-literal variable passed by name to subprocess.run), and recommends deleting the timing assertion outright plus extending the AST scanner to resolve simple same-scope string-variable bindings passed to subprocess/exec-style calls, with a synthetic self-test since no other real instance of the shape exists in the tree.

next_steps: Run /plan 213 to create an implementation plan covering: (1) delete the wall-clock assertion and its now-dead supporting lines from test_import_performs_no_subprocess_call's injected subprocess source; (2) extend test_timing_marker_coverage.py's AST scan to resolve same-function string-literal variables passed to subprocess/exec-style calls and recursively apply the existing clock-read/bound-assert detectors, with a synthetic self-test proving both the positive and marker-suppressed negative cases; (3) verify with one clean full-gate -n 4 run plus the scanner's own test suite.

memory_candidates.content: AST-based timing-marker scanners (code/tests/ci/test_timing_marker_coverage.py style) only see literal source text as an opaque ast.Constant when a test embeds Python code in a string handed to subprocess.run/exec/eval -- including when the string is first bound to a local variable and referenced by name inside a list literal (e.g. [sys.executable, "-c", code]). Extending such a scanner requires resolving same-scope simple string-variable bindings and re-parsing/re-scanning the resolved string, not just scanning literal call arguments directly.
